sentences.text: It's true that high-school coding classes aren't essential for learning computer science in college.

sentences.text: Students without experience can catch up after a few introductory courses, said Tom Cortina, the assistant dean at Carnegie Mellon's School of Computer Science.
However, Cortina said, early exposure is beneficial.
sentences.translation: 然而,Cortina说,早期接触是有益的。当年幼的孩子学习计算机科学时,他们会了解到这不仅仅是令人困惑的、无穷无尽的字母和数字串,而是构建应用程序、创作艺术作品或检验假设的工具。对他们来说,转变思维过程并不像对年龄较大的学生那样困难。将问题分解成小块并使用代码解决它们成为常态。Cortina说,让更多儿童接受这种训练可以增加对该领域感兴趣的人数,并有助于填补就业缺口。

sentences.text: When younger kids learn computer science, they learn that it's not just a confusing, endless string of letters and numbers – but a tool to build apps, or create artwork, or test hypotheses.
It's not as hard for them to transform their thought processes as it is for older students.
Breaking down problems into bite-sized chunks and using code to solve them becomes normal.
Giving more children this training could increase the number of people interested in the field and help fill the jobs gap, Cortina said.

Students also benefit from learning something about coding before they get to college, where introductory computer-science classes are packed to the brim, which can drive the less-experienced or less-determined students away.

sentences.text: The reason for this is simple: The longer you stay in the store, the more stuff you'll see, and the more stuff you see, the more you'll buy.
And supermarkets contain a lot of stuff.
The average supermarket, according to the Food Marketing Institute, carries some 44,000 different items, and many carry tens of thousands more.
The sheer volume of available choice is enough to send shoppers into a state of information overload.
According to brain-scan experiments, the demands of so much decision- making quickly become too much for us.

After about 40 minutes of shopping, most people stop struggling to be rationally selective, and instead begin shopping emotionally – which is the point at which we accumulate the 50 percent of stuff in our cart that we never intended buying.

translation.content:
P1 The supermarket is designed to lure customers into spending as much time as possible within its
doors. The reason for this is simple: The longer you stay in the store, the more stuff you'll see, and the
more stuff you see, the more you'll buy. And supermarkets contain a lot of stuff. The average
supermarket, according to the Food Marketing Institute, carries some 44,000 different items, and many
carry tens of thousands more. The sheer volume of available choice is enough to send shoppers into a
state of information overload. According to brain-scan experiments, the demands of so much decision-
making quickly become too much for us. After about 40 minutes of shopping, most people stop
struggling to be rationally selective, and instead begin shopping emotionally – which is the point at
which we accumulate the 50 percent of stuff in our cart that we never intended buying.

协会称，一家普通超市经营着约 44000 种不同的商品，许多超市经营的种类还要多出数万种。可供选

开始凭情绪购物——而正是在这时，我们把购物车里那 50% 自己从没打算买的商品堆积了起来。

part_a.directions:
Read the following four texts. Answer the questions after each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark
your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)
Text 1
P1 It's true that high-school coding classes aren't essential for learning computer science in college.
Students without experience can catch up after a few introductory courses, said Tom Cortina, the
assistant dean at Carnegie Mellon's School of Computer Science.
诚然,高中编程课程对于在大学学习计算机科学并非必不可少。卡内基梅隆大学计算机科学学院的副院长
Tom Cortina表示,没有经验的学生在学习几门入门课程后就能赶上进度。
P2 However, Cortina said, early exposure is beneficial. When younger kids learn computer science,
they learn that it's not just a confusing, endless string of letters and numbers – but a tool to build apps,
or create artwork, or test hypotheses. It's not as hard for them to transform their thought processes as it
is for older students. Breaking down problems into bite-sized chunks and using code to solve them
becomes normal. Giving more children this training could increase the number of people interested in the
field and help fill the jobs gap, Cortina said.
然而,Cortina说,早期接触是有益的。当年幼的孩子学习计算机科学时,他们会了解到这不仅仅是令人困惑
的、无穷无尽的字母和数字串,而是构建应用程序、创作艺术作品或检验假设的工具。对他们来说,转变思
维过程并不像对年龄较大的学生那样困难。将问题分解成小块并使用代码解决它们成为常态。Cortina说,
让更多儿童接受这种训练可以增加对该领域感兴趣的人数,并有助于填补就业缺口。
P3 Students also benefit from learning something about coding before they get to college, where
introductory computer-science classes are packed to the brim, which can drive the less-experienced or
less-determined students away.
学生在上大学之前学习一些编程知识也会受益,因为大学的计算机科学入门课程人满为患,这可能会让经验
较少或决心不够坚定的学生望而却步。

P4 The Flatiron School, where people pay to learn programming, started as one of the many coding
bootcamps that have become popular for adults looking for a career change. The high-schoolers get the
same curriculum, but "we try to gear lessons toward things they're interested in," said Victoria Friedman,
an instructor. For instance, one of the apps the students are developing suggests movies based on your
mood.
Flatiron School是一所人们付费学习编程的学校,最初是众多编程训练营之一,这些训练营在寻求职业转变
的成年人中变得流行起来。高中生接受同样的课程,但教师Victoria Friedman说,"我们试图让课程面向他
们感兴趣的事物"。例如,学生正在开发的一个应用程序根据你的心情推荐电影。
P5 The students in the Flatiron class probably won't drop out of high school and build the next
Facebook. Programming languages have a quick turnover, so the "Ruby on Rails" language they learned
may not even be relevant by the time they enter the job market. But the skills they learn – how to think
logically through a problem and organize the results – apply to any coding language, said Deborah
Seehorn, an education consultant for the state of North Carolina.
Flatiron班级的学生可能不会从高中辍学去创建下一个Facebook。编程语言更新换代很快,因此他们学习
的Ruby on Rails语言到他们进入就业市场时甚至可能已经不再相关。但北卡罗来纳州教育顾问Deborah
Seehorn说,他们学到的技能——如何从逻辑上思考问题并组织结果——适用于任何编程语言。
P6 Indeed, the Flatiron students might not go into IT at all. But creating a future army of coders is
not the sole purpose of the classes. These kids are going to be surrounded by computers – in their
pockets, in their offices, in their homes – for the rest of their lives. The younger they learn how
computers think, how to coax the machine into producing what they want – the earlier they learn that
they have the power to do that – the better.
事实上,Flatiron的学生可能根本不会进入IT行业。但培养未来的程序员大军并非这些课程的唯一目的。这
些孩子在他们余生中都将被计算机包围——在他们的口袋里、办公室里、家里。他们越早学会计算机如何
思考,如何哄骗机器产出他们想要的东西——越早学会他们有能力做到这一点——就越好。

21.Cortina holds that early exposure to computer science makes it easier to____.
[ A ]complete future job training
[ B ]remodel the way of thinking
[ C ]formulate logical hypotheses
[ D ]perfect artwork production
Cortina认为早期接触计算机科学使得____变得更容易。
A) 完成未来的职业培训 B) 重塑思维方式 C) 制定逻辑假设 D) 完善艺术作品制作
【答案】B （细节题）
【判型】题干 Cortina holds that early exposure to computer science makes it easier to 直接问
Cortina 持有的具体观点，是对原文一个具体陈述的转述题。
【拆句】Cortina holds that early exposure to computer science makes it easier to____：主句
Cortina holds that...，宾语从句中 early exposure 是主语，makes it easier to do 是 "使
做某事更容易" 的形式宾语结构，it 指代后接的 to 不定式。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】When younger kids learn computer science, they learn that it's not just a confusing, endless
string of letters and numbers – but a tool to build apps, or create artwork, or test hypotheses.
It's not as hard for them to transform their thought processes as it is for older students.
当年幼的孩子学习计算机科学时，他们会明白它不只是令人困惑的、没完没了的字母与数字
串——而是用来开发应用、创作艺术作品或检验假设的工具。对他们来说，改变思维方式不
像对年纪大些的学生那样困难。
【选项】A) 无中生有
complete future job training 在原文 Cortina 关于 early exposure 的论述中找不到
对应——P2 只谈 thought processes 和 jobs gap，未提任何 "完成未来职业培训" 的
内容。
B) ✓ 正确
transform their thought processes ↔ remodel the way of thinking
预判 "改变思维方式更容易" 与 remodel the way of thinking 在动作与宾语上一一对
应，锁定 B。
C) 偷换概念
原文 test hypotheses 是说编程可以"检验假设"，是工具的一种用法举例；选项
formulate logical hypotheses 偷换为"形成逻辑假设"，动作从"检验"换成了"提出"，对
象从 "hypotheses" 加了 "logical" 限定。
D) 偷换概念
原文 create artwork 同样是编程的用途举例；选项 perfect artwork production 把
create（创作）替换成 perfect（使完美），还加了 production，与原文不符。

[ B ]interest

英语二真题(2016)
Section II Part A (3)
Directions:
Read the following four texts. Answer the questions after each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark
your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)
Text 3
P1 That everyone's too busy these days is a cliché. But one specific complaint is made especially
mournfully: There's never any time to read.
如今每个人都太忙了,这已是陈词滥调。但有一种抱怨尤其令人哀伤:永远没有时间阅读。
P2 What makes the problem thornier is that the usual time-management techniques don't seem
sufficient. The web's full of articles offering tips on making time to read: "Give up TV" or "Carry a
book with you at all times." But in my experience, using such methods to free up the odd 30 minutes
doesn't work. Sit down to read and the flywheel of work-related thoughts keeps spinning – or else you're
so exhausted that a challenging book's the last thing you need. The modern mind, Tim Parks, a novelist
and critic, writes, "is overwhelmingly inclined toward communication… It is not simply that one is
interrupted; it is that one is actually inclined to interruption." Deep reading requires not just time, but a
special kind of time which can't be obtained merely by becoming more efficient.
让这个问题更棘手的是,通常的时间管理技巧似乎并不够用。网上充斥着提供腾出时间阅读建议的文章:"放
弃看电视"或"随时随地带本书"。但根据我的经验,用这些方法来挤出零星的30分钟并不奏效。坐下来阅读
时,与工作相关的思绪飞轮依然转个不停——要么就是你疲惫不堪,一本有挑战性的书是你最不需要的东
西。小说家兼评论家Tim Parks写道,现代人的思维"压倒性地倾向于交流……问题不仅仅在于一个人被打断;
而在于一个人实际上倾向于被打断"。深度阅读不仅需要时间,还需要一种特殊的时间,这种时间无法仅仅通
过提高效率来获得。
P3 In fact, "becoming more efficient" is part of the problem. Thinking of time as a resource to be
maximised means you approach it instrumentally, judging any given moment as well spent only in so far
as it advances progress toward some goal. Immersive reading, by contrast, depends on being willing to
risk inefficiency, goallessness, even time-wasting. Try to slot it in as a to-do list item and you'll manage
懒笔记 · https://english-exam.lazynote.cn/kaoyan/sections/2016-english-two/section2-part-a-3/?f=p · 在线使⽤效果更好
only goal-focused reading – useful, sometimes, but not the most fulfilling kind. "The future comes at us
like empty bottles along an unstoppable and nearly infinite conveyor belt," writes Gary Eberle in his
book Sacred Time, and "we feel a pressure to fill these different-sized bottles (days, hours, minutes) as
they pass, for if they get by without being filled, we will have wasted them." No mind-set could be
worse for losing yourself in a book.
事实上,"提高效率"本身就是问题的一部分。把时间视为需要最大化利用的资源,意味着你会工具性地对待
它,仅仅根据某个时刻是否推进了某个目标的进展来判断它是否被妥善利用。相比之下,沉浸式阅读依赖于
愿意冒无效率、无目标甚至浪费时间的风险。试图把它作为待办事项清单中的一项塞进去,你只能做到目标
导向的阅读——有时有用,但不是最令人满足的那种。Gary Eberle在其著作《神圣时间》中写道:"未来像
空瓶子一样沿着一条无法停止且几乎无限的传送带向我们涌来","我们感到一种压力,要在这些不同大小的
瓶子(天、小时、分钟)经过时填满它们,因为如果它们没被填满就过去了,我们就浪费了它们"。没有哪种心
态比这更不利于让自己沉浸在一本书中。
P4 So what does work? Perhaps surprisingly, scheduling regular times for reading. You'd think this
might fuel the efficiency mind-set, but in fact, Eberle notes, such ritualistic behaviour helps us "step
outside time's flow" into "soul time." You could limit distractions by reading only physical books, or on
single-purpose e-readers. "Carry a book with you at all times" can actually work, too – providing you
dip in often enough, so that reading becomes the default state from which you temporarily surface to
take care of business, before dropping back down. On a really good day, it no longer feels as if you're
"making time to read," but just reading, and making time for everything else.
那么什么方法有效呢?或许令人惊讶的是,安排固定的阅读时间。你可能会认为这会助长效率心态,但事实
上,Eberle指出,这种仪式化行为帮助我们"走出时间的流动"进入"灵魂时间"。你可以通过只阅读纸质书或专
用电子阅读器来减少干扰。"随时随地带本书"实际上也能奏效——只要你足够频繁地翻阅,让阅读成为默认
状态,你只是暂时从中浮出水面来处理事务,然后再沉回去。在真正美好的一天,你不再觉得自己是在"腾出时
间阅读",而只是在阅读,并为其他一切事情腾出时间。

Section II Part B
Directions:
Read the following text and answer the questions by choosing the most suitable subheading from the list
A-G for each of the numbered paragraphs (41-45). There are two extra subheadings which you do not
need to use. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)
As adults, it seems that we are constantly pursuing happiness, often with mixed results. Yet children
appear to have it down to an art – and for the most part they don't need self-help books or therapy.
Instead, they look after their wellbeing instinctively, and usually more effectively than we do as
grownups. Perhaps it's time to learn a few lessons from them.
作为成年人,我们似乎一直在追求幸福,但结果往往好坏参半。然而孩子们似乎已经将此变成了一门艺术
——而且在大多数情况下,他们不需要自助书籍或心理治疗。相反,他们本能地照顾自己的幸福感,而且通常
比我们成年人做得更有效。也许是时候向他们学习一些经验了。
(41)____________________
表达你的情绪
What does a child do when he's sad? He cries. When he's angry? He shouts. Scared? Probably a bit
of both. As we grow up, we learn to control our emotions so they are manageable and don't dictate our
behaviours, which is in many ways a good thing. But too often we take this process too far and end up
suppressing emotions, especially negative ones. That's about as effective as brushing dirt under a carpet
and can even make us ill. What we need to do is find a way to acknowledge and express what we feel
appropriately, and then – again, like children – move on.
当孩子悲伤时他会做什么?他会哭。当他生气时呢?他会大喊。害怕时呢?可能两者兼有。随着我们长大,我
们学会控制自己的情绪,使它们变得可控且不会支配我们的行为,这在很多方面是件好事。但我们往往把这
个过程推得太远,最终压抑情绪,尤其是负面情绪。这就像把灰尘扫到地毯下一样无效,甚至可能让我们生
病。我们需要做的是找到一种方法来恰当地承认和表达我们的感受,然后——再次像孩子一样——继续
前进。

容易满足
A couple of Christmases ago, my youngest stepdaughter, who was nine years old at the time, got a
Superman T-shirt for Christmas. It cost less than a fiver but she was overjoyed, and couldn't stop talking

表现得傻乎乎
Have you ever noticed how much children laugh? If we adults could indulge in a bit of silliness
and giggling, we would reduce the stress hormones in our bodies, increase good hormones like
endorphins, improve blood flow to our hearts and even have a greater chance of fighting off infection.
All of which would, of course, have a positive effect on our happiness levels.
你有没有注意到孩子们笑得有多频繁?如果我们成年人能够沉浸在一点傻乎乎和咯咯笑中,我们就能减少体
内的压力激素,增加像内啡肽这样的有益激素,改善心脏的血液流动,甚至有更大的机会抵抗感染。所有这些
当然会对我们的幸福水平产生积极影响。
(44)____________________
享受乐趣
The problem with being a grownup is that there's an awful lot of serious stuff to deal with – work,
mortgage payments, figuring out what to cook for dinner. But as adults we also have the luxury of being
able to control our own diaries and it's important that we schedule in time to enjoy the things we love.
Those things might be social, sporting, creative or completely random (dancing around the living room,
anyone?) – it doesn't matter, so long as they're enjoyable, and not likely to have negative side effects,
such as drinking too much alcohol or going on a wild spending spree if you're on a tight budget.
成为成年人的问题在于有大量严肃的事情要处理——工作、抵押贷款、想清楚晚饭做什么。但作为成年
人,我们也拥有能够控制自己日程安排的奢侈,重要的是我们要安排时间去享受我们热爱的事物。这些事情
可能是社交的、体育的、创造性的或完全随机的(在客厅里跳舞,有人愿意吗?)——这无关紧要,只要它们是
令人愉快的,并且不太可能产生负面副作用,比如在预算紧张的情况下喝太多酒或疯狂消费。

goal but a natural byproduct of the way they live.

Directions:

doors. The reason for this is simple: The longer you stay in the store, the more stuff you'll see, and the
more stuff you see, the more you'll buy. And supermarkets contain a lot of stuff. The average
supermarket, according to the Food Marketing Institute, carries some 44,000 different items, and many

state of information overload. According to brain-scan experiments, the demands of so much decision-

开始凭情绪购物——而正是在这时，我们把购物车里那 50% 自己从没打算买的商品堆积了起来。

carries some 44,000 different items：carry 在零售语境里不是「携带」，而是「（商店）经
营、销售、备有（某种商品）」；some 放在数字前是「大约」，不是「一些」。两处都是易看
走眼的熟词僻义。
and many carry tens of thousands more.（并列分句）★采分→而许多超市经营的还要多出数
万种。
难点：many 省略中心词 + more 的比较
many carry tens of thousands more 中 many 后省略了 supermarkets，指「许多超市」；
more 是与前面 44000 比较，意为「（比这）还多数万种」。tens of thousands 是「数万」。

把插入语 according to the Food Marketing Institute 提到句首译成「据食品营销协会称」；这
样主语「一家普通超市」和谓语「经营约 44000 种商品」就重新接拢，句子顺了。
【译文】据食品营销协会称，一家普通超市经营着约 44000 种不同的商品，许多超市经营的
种类还要多出数万种。
5. The sheer volume of available choice is enough to send shoppers into a state of
information overload.
【意群】The sheer volume of available choice（主干主语（含介词短语作定语））★采分→可供选择的纯
粹数量
难点：sheer volume / available choice 抽象名词具体化
The sheer volume of available choice：sheer 是「纯粹的、十足的」起强调，volume 此处是
「数量、量」，available choice 是「可供选择的（商品）」。整块意思是「可供选择的商品数
量之大」，把抽象名词堆叠译成「（商品）选择之多」更顺。
is enough to send shoppers into a state of information overload.（谓语 + 结果（be enough to
do））★采分→足以把购物者送入一种信息过载的状态。
难点：send sb into a state + information overload
send shoppers into a state of information overload：send… into a state of 不是「送
进」，是「使……陷入……状态」；information overload 是固定术语「信息过载/信息超载」，
指信息多到大脑处理不过来。is enough to 译「足以」。
【调序】of 后置定语前移 + send into 转「使陷入」
of available choice 是后置修饰 volume 的，提到前面译「可供选择的商品（数量）」；谓语
send shoppers into a state of information overload 转成「使购物者陷入信息过载的状态」，
把英文的「送入」改成中文的「使……陷入」。
【译文】可供选择的商品数量之大，足以使购物者陷入信息过载的状态。

6. According to brain-scan experiments, the demands of so much decision-making quickly become
too much for us.
【意群】According to brain-scan experiments,（来源状语（句首））→据脑部扫描实验，
难点：brain-scan 复合词直译
brain-scan experiments 是复合名词「脑部扫描实验」，brain-scan 作定语修饰
experiments，直接译「脑部扫描实验」即可，无难点，但要确保译出来源含义「据……（实
验）表明」。
the demands of so much decision-making（主干主语（含 of 定语））★采分→如此多决策的
要求
难点：demands / decision-making 抽象名词具体化
the demands of so much decision-making：demands 是「（对人的）要求、负担、消
耗」，decision-making 是「做决定、决策」。整块直译「如此多决策的要求」生硬，意思是
「要做这么多决定所带来的负担」，需具体化。
quickly become too much for us.（谓语 + 表语（too much for sb））★采分→很快变得对我们
来说太多了。
难点：too much for us 译「让我们吃不消」
become too much for us：too much for sb 是固定表达「让某人难以承受、吃不消、应付不
来」，不是字面「对我们太多」。这是采分点，直译会丢掉「承受不了」的核心意思。
【调序】of 定语前移 + 致使义意译
of so much decision-making 提到 demands 前，译「要做这么多决定（所带来的）负担」；
表语 too much for us 意译为「让我们难以承受/吃不消」，把英文的「太多」转成中文的「承受
不了」。
【译文】脑部扫描实验表明，要做这么多决定所带来的负担，很快就会让我们吃不消。

7. After about 40 minutes of shopping, most people stop struggling to be rationally selective, and
instead begin shopping emotionally – which is the point at which we accumulate the 50 percent of
stuff in our cart that we never intended buying.
【意群】After about 40 minutes of shopping,（时间状语（句首））→购物约 40 分钟后，
难点：时间状语直译即可
After about 40 minutes of shopping 是时间状语，直译「购物大约 40 分钟之后」，about 表
约数「大约」，放句首，无难点。
most people stop struggling to be rationally selective,（主干主谓宾（stop doing））★采分→大
多数人停止努力做到理性地挑选，
难点：stop struggling to be selective 的层层含义
stop struggling to be rationally selective：stop doing 是「停止做某事」；struggle to do
是「努力、挣扎着去做」；rationally selective 是「理性地有选择（地买）」。合起来即「不再
努力保持理性的挑选」，三层意思要都译出，是关键采分意群。
and instead begin shopping emotionally（并列谓语（and instead））★采分→反而开始情绪化
地购物
难点：instead 的转折对照
and instead begin shopping emotionally：instead 在此是「反而、转而」，与前半句「不再
理性挑选」形成对照——从理性转向情绪化。emotionally 译「凭情绪、感情用事地」购物。
– which is the point at which we accumulate the 50 percent of stuff in our cart（非限定定语从句
（which 回指前句））★采分→——这正是我们把购物车里 50% 的商品堆积起来的时刻
难点：which 回指 + the point at which 双重从句
破折号后的 which 不指某个名词，而是回指前面「开始情绪化购物」这整件事，译「而这时/这
一刻」；the point at which… 是「……的时刻/这时候」，at which 引导定语从句修饰 the
point。stuff in our cart 即「购物车里的商品」。
that we never intended buying.（定语从句（that 修饰 stuff））★采分→那些是我们从没打算
买的
难点：that 回指 stuff + never intended 含否定
that we never intended buying：that 是定语从句的关系词，修饰前面的 stuff（商品）；
never intended buying 是「从来没打算/没想要买的」，含 never 这个含蓄否定，是全句点睛
——这 50% 的商品本不在购买计划内，照应全文「被诱导多买」的主旨。
【调序】定语从句拆成分句 + 否定前置修饰
which 从句较长，不前移，独立译成「而这时……」一个分句；最后 that we never intended
buying 是修饰 stuff 的定语，提到 stuff 前译「我们从没打算买的（那些商品）」，让「50% 的商
品」和「从没打算买」紧贴。
【译文】购物大约 40 分钟之后，大多数人就不再努力保持理性的挑选，反而开始凭情绪购物
——而正是在这时，我们把购物车里那 50% 自己从没打算买的商品堆积了起来。

Section IV Part A
Directions:
Suppose you won a translation contest and your friend, Jack, wrote an email to congratulate you and
ask for advice on translation. Write him a reply to
1)thank him, and
2)give your advice.
You should write about 100 words on the ANSWER SHEET.

Dear Jack,
Thank you so much for your warm congratulations on my winning the translation contest. Your kind words
mean a lot to me, and I am truly delighted to share the good news with a friend like you.
As for translation, here are a few tips I found helpful. First, read plenty of bilingual texts and collect fixed
expressions, which sharpen your sense of both languages. Second, understand the whole sentence before you
start, rather than translating word by word. Finally, keep practising and revising your drafts, since skill grows
only through steady effort.
